long_biography.plain_text:
At Coram's Tehachapi wind project, Brian O'Sullivan replaced ageing small turbines with modern machines and confronted a second obstacle: limited transmission capacity. As president, he argued that new generation could not reach customers unless the grid could carry it. He also represented the California Wind Energy Association in utility proceedings over renewable-power contracts.

Utility-scale battery storage added a new operating problem for Coram: holding surplus wind and solar output until the grid required it. This made renewable generation more dependable. Coram selected long-duration, modular technology that could move stored electricity from periods of excess production to periods of customer demand.
